protocol.unit: the rewrite as written in the candidate RTL (for nonequiv candidates: what the RTL actually does, not the intention)
protocol.c2: the cycle-level timing of an output changes: pipeline stages added or removed, or outputs that were registered are produced combinationally from the state (for nonequiv candidates this is a judgment; the lock-step offset is only measured on candidates that pass V2)
protocol.c1: latency preserved, registers cross combinational logic (retiming-style): registers removed, added or merged such that logic that sat before a register now sits after it or vice versa, e.g. output registers replaced by a decode of a delayed state register, pipeline registers merged across an adder level, an FSM re-scheduled to absorb its output delay
protocol.d: the algorithm, datapath organisation, buffer organisation or schedule is different: another arithmetic algorithm (shift-add mux tree vs `*`, explicit ripple carry vs carry-lookahead / prefix network vs behavioural `+`, radix-2 vs radix-4 partial products), another storage organisation (indexed memory vs shift-register stack vs pointer-addressed write), another control schedule (FSM plus counter vs one phase counter)
protocol.b: latency-preserving coding / structural refactor that changes the register structure or the stored state without moving registers across logic: always-block split or merge, state encoding, bit-width reduction, redundant-register removal (a register replaced by a function of other registers), removal of unobservable state updates (reset or clear of an unread memory entry), register split / array flattening, enables added
protocol.a: the state elements (registers and memories: names, widths, reset behaviour, update conditions, stored values at every cycle) are unchanged and only the combinational logic is re-expressed (case vs if/else recoding of next-state logic, mux restructuring, operator recoding, constant folding), wherever the text sits
protocol.note: Where the spec 04 A.1 definition names a transformation explicitly (always-block merge/split, state encoding, bit width, precomputation, strength reduction -> b) the named class wins; the state-element criterion decides the rest.
